entries.parental rights and responsibilities: the court's decisions about who makes major decisions for a child and where the child lives
entries.primary residence: the place where a child lives most of the time
entries.contact schedule: the planned times a child spends with a parent or other person
entries.child support: money a parent may be ordered to pay to help support a child
entries.parentage: the legal relationship between a child and a parent
entries.motion to modify: a request asking the court to change an existing order
entries.motion to enforce: a request asking the court to require compliance with an order
entries.contempt: a claim that someone willfully disobeyed a court order
entries.protection from abuse: a court process that can provide safety-related orders
entries.guardian ad litem: a person appointed to help the court with information about a child's interests
entries.rule 52 findings: written findings that explain the facts and reasoning behind a court decision
entries.best interest factors: the factors Maine courts review when deciding what arrangement serves a child's best interests
entries.service: the formal delivery of court papers to another person
entries.jurisdiction: the court's legal power to decide a case
entries.affidavit: a written statement signed under oath
entries.proposed order: a draft order someone asks the judge to sign
entries.filing-ready: ready to file only after all required checks and human review are complete
entries.review required: a person still needs to review this before relying on it
entries.source verified: the source has been checked and identified with enough detail to rely on it more safely
entries.unsupported claim: a statement that does not yet have enough verified source support
